core_obligations: Identify (a)<=>(b) with the definition, and (a)<=>(e), (a)<=>(f) with parts of lemma-etale-smooth-local-source-target-implies; conclude (a)<=>(g) formally (proof lines 3279-3286).

Prove (c) implies (b) trivially and (b) implies (c) by coproducting the charts h_x : U_x \to V_x over all x, noting the coproduct h has P because {V_x \to \coprod V_x} is a smooth covering and P is smooth local on the target (proof lines 3288-3298).

Prove (a) implies (d): for any diagram as in (d), X \times_Y V \to V has P by smooth base change and U \to V has P by \'etale precomposition stability; prove (d) implies (a) by taking U = X, V = Y (proof lines 3300-3307).
proof_roadmap: Pin (a), (b), (e), (f), (g) together through the definition and the permanence lemma.
Build the type-(c) diagram as a coproduct of the local charts from (b).
Handle the universal diagram (d) by base change plus precomposition stability, and recover (a) from the trivial diagram.
difficulty_reason: The proof runs a seven-way equivalence chase: (a)<=>(b) is the definition itself; (a)<=>(e) and (a)<=>(f) come from the permanence lemma's parts; (g) then follows formally; (c)<=> (b) needs a genuine construction — from (b) take the coproduct over x of the charts to build a diagram of type (c), using smooth locality on the target to see the coproduct h has P; finally (d): from (a), any diagram as in (d) has X \times_Y V \to V with P by smooth base change, so U \to V has P by \'etale precomposition stability; conversely (d) with U = X, V = Y gives (a). The web of reductions across seven statements is the substance.
